problem: Given $X∼B(6,0.2),$ compute $P(3\le X\le 5).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(6,0.2),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x})(0.2)^{x}(0.8)^{6-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3\le X\le 5) & =P(X\in {3,4,5}) \\  & =f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{3})(0.2)^{3}(0.8)^{6-3}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{4})(0.2)^{4}(0.8)^{6-4}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{5})(0.2)^{5}(0.8)^{6-5} \\  & =20(0.2)^{3}(0.8)^{3}+15(0.2)^{4}(0.8)^{2}+6(0.2)^{5}(0.8) \\  & ≈0.0988\end{aligned}
$$

to $4$ decimal places.
